bluf: El Niño is strengthening (FEWS NET, Oct 21) and is the common driver behind today's top WATINT threats. 1) Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen and Somalia stack conflict, drought or flood, and famine risk: Sudan has 19.5M people in IPC Phase 3+ and 12.9M forcibly displaced; IOM projects 874,319 Somalis could be displaced Oct-Dec, 92% by flooding; Yemen's renewed fighting has displaced 256,591 people (IOM DTM via WHO, Oct 19) and UNICEF warns Taiz water for 1.6M children is at risk. 2) GDACS carries five Orange agricultural droughts (Central and East Africa, Central America and the Caribbean, Europe) and a Red typhoon, CHAMPI-26, over the Philippines, Guam and Japan. 3) Food and protein: Oxfam reports 62M people in eastern and southern Africa facing worsening food insecurity and more than 70,000 Central American farm households with maize losses; FAO reports degraded pasture and crop water stress in Yemen. 4) Energy: hydro-heavy grids (Ethiopia 97%, Sudan 83%, Afghanistan 72% of electricity) are exposed to rainfall deficits, and Telangana, India expects an El Niño water and power crisis until July. 5) Homeland: 50.7% of CONUS is in moderate or worse drought (USDM, Oct 20) while flash floods hit the Four Corners.

notes.YEM: Renewed West Coast and Shabwah fighting is driving displacement and threatens Taiz water supply. Its position on Bab el-Mandeb ties water-driven instability to Red Sea shipping and CENTCOM force protection. Watch: cholera, more arrivals in Djibouti (3,836 by Oct 17, IOM).
notes.SYR: Very high water stress (Aqueduct 4.01) and 5.5M IDPs. Euphrates and Tigris flows and dam control remain leverage for state and non-state actors where US forces and partners operate. Watch: wheat shortfalls and upstream dam releases.
notes.SDN: El Niño drought and famine risk on top of the SAF-RSF war. The grid is 83% hydro, so Nile flows and GERD operations feed straight into power supply. Outflows strain Chad, Egypt, South Sudan and Ethiopia and complicate Red Sea stability and partner mediation.
notes.HTI: Inside the GDACS Orange Caribbean drought, with 5.7M in IPC 3+ and displacement driven by gang violence. Maritime migration toward the US is the main homeland link, and late-season storms add flood risk.
notes.SSD: Highest INFORM risk in the set (8.5). Flooding persists in the Sudd and Bentiu while the south dries out, and Oxfam reports nearly 8M acutely food insecure. Watch: spillover from Sudan and oil exports that depend on the pipeline to Port Sudan.
notes.ERI: Sits inside the GDACS Orange Sahel and Horn drought belt, with very little data (no current IPC or DTM figures). Its Red Sea coastline makes drought-driven instability relevant to the shipping corridor. Low confidence.
notes.UKR: Water infrastructure is a recurring target: the Pacific Institute lists 159 Ukraine-linked entries for 2020-2025. A local ceasefire for aid and evacuation in Oleshky was reported on Oct 23. Watch: Dnipro supply to the southern oblasts and how power and water outages compound each other in winter.
notes.AFG: 15.9M people in IPC 3+ (analysis to Oct 2026) and 3.2M IDPs. The Qosh Tepa canal on the Amu Darya and Helmand flows are cross-border friction points with Central Asia and Iran, and FEWS NET flags a flood threat in the east.
notes.MEX: High water stress (4.0), the Orange regional drought and Tropical Cyclone VANCE-26. Rio Grande and Colorado deliveries under the 1944 treaty, plus the Four Corners floods, make this the most direct WATINT link to the US homeland.
notes.IND: High water stress (4.11). Telangana expects its El Niño water and power crisis to last until July, and anti-dam protests in Arunachal's Siang region touch the India-China contest over the Brahmaputra. Watch: rabi planting and power load-shedding.
notes.SOM: IOM and DRC project 874,319 displaced Oct-Dec, 92% by flooding, and FEWS NET reports Shabelle gauges above high flood risk. Displacement that al-Shabaab can exploit, plus aid access, are force-protection and CT concerns.
notes.ETH: The grid is 97% hydro. WFP reports El Niño rainfall deficits in Tigray, Amhara, Afar and eastern Oromia, all inside the GDACS Orange East Africa drought. Nile and GERD diplomacy with Egypt and Sudan is the main strategic lever.
notes.IRN: Extreme water stress (4.65) amid renewed regional hostilities that IOM says are disrupting services and infrastructure (Oct 22). Water and power shortfalls drive domestic instability, and Gulf dependence on desalination raises regional infrastructure risk.
